title: RAP-Track: Efficient Control Flow Attestation via Parallel Tracking in Commodity MCUs
problem: Control flow attestation (CFA) for safety-critical embedded systems requires remote verification of program execution paths, but current approaches suffer from high performance overhead due to code instrumentation and frequent context switches.
motivation: Safety-critical embedded systems (industrial control, medical devices) need runtime verification; reducing CFA overhead is essential for practical deployment without compromising security.
method: Leverages commodity hardware extensions—Micro Trace Buffer (MTB) and Data Watchpoint and Trace Unit (DWT)—to track control flow paths in parallel with program execution, avoiding instrumentation overhead and context switches. Implements prototype on open-source systems.
key_novelty: First practical use of commodity MTB and DWT hardware trace buffers for parallel control flow tracking, eliminating instrumentation overhead and achieving efficient CFA for embedded systems.
contributions: Hardware-based parallel control flow tracking using MTB/DWT
Elimination of instrumentation and context-switch overhead
Substantial performance gains over state-of-the-art CFA
Enhanced practicality and security of embedded system attestation

metrics.other: Performance improvement (specific metrics not detailed in abstract)

limitations: Evaluation on specific MCU architecture; applicability to other embedded platforms and hardware without MTB/DWT not discussed.
primary_theme: Hardware-assisted control flow attestation for embedded systems
